text:
sasha: heads-up — ran a quick cross-dataset sanity for the new reranker (xpt-2.1q-int8). noticing bigger quality delta on LegalDocs than on WebQA. wondering if this is dataset-shift or quantization fragility.
sasha: baseline fp16 vs int8 snippets below. full eval command i used at the bottom.
cheng: can you paste the numbers?
sasha: here, ndcg@10 / mrr (rounded):
```
baseline_fp16: webqa ndcg@10=0.421, mrr=0.375
baseline_fp16: legal ndcg@10=0.388, mrr=0.342
quant_int8:    webqa ndcg@10=0.412, mrr=0.369
quant_int8:    legal ndcg@10=0.360, mrr=0.311
after_isotonic_calib_on_holdout: legal ndcg@10=0.379, mrr=0.333
p-values (paired bootstrap): webqa drop p=0.22, legal drop p=0.028
```

maria: interesting — the legal drop is substantial and statistically significant. did you use the same doc truncation / tokenizer pipeline for both datasets? LegalDocs often has long context and metadata that change the score distribution.

sasha: same pipeline, but LegalDocs has longer docs and more label imbalance (lots of near-duplicates in positives). i suspect calibration/score shift rather than pure ranker recall loss.

ben: two quick checks: 1) run importance reweighting so dataset doc length distribution matches webqa, 2) check top-1 vs top-10 drift per query bucket. might reveal whether it's a calibration offset or ordering mistakes.

vivek: also try swapping encoders: run the quantized reranker but leave the encoder fp16 (hybrid) to see if quantization in the scoring head is the culprit. magnet: quantization noise often amplifies when queries are out-of-distribution.

sasha: good call. i ran a cheap ablation: quantize-only-scorer (encoder fp16, scorer int8) -> legal ndcg@10=0.367 (partial recovery). full int8 worse.

maria: suggests we need transfer-aware calibration: train an isotonic regression on a small holdout from target distribution (legal) and apply post-hoc. that's what boosted you from 0.360 to 0.379. we should test sample efficiency of that calibration.

sasha: agree. i did a sweep: calibration holdout sizes 100 / 500 / 2000 queries -> legal ndcg@10 after calib: 0.368 / 0.376 / 0.379. diminishing returns after ~500.

ben: good metric to add to onboarding checklist: "calibration holdout size needed per domain". also add a quick check for label noise — run exact-match deduping on positives; duplicates can inflate baseline and make drops look worse.

vivek: for significance, use stratified bootstrap by query (not by document) and report both mean delta and 95% CI. also track per-query variance distribution (histogram of ndcg change per query) to spot heavy tails.

sasha: plan proposed:
- run hybrid encoder ablation across webqa/legal/docs
- run importance-reweighted eval to match retrieval doc length distribution
- collect calibration holdout of 500 on legal and test isotonic/platt scaling
- bootstrap with 10k resamples stratified by query and report p & CI

sasha: eval command i used (for reproducibility):
```
python eval_rerank.py \
  --model xpt-2.1q-int8 \
  --datasets webqa,legal,docs \
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr \
  --calib-split 0.1 \
  --dedupe-positives true \
  --seed 42
```

ci-bot: test run finished: uploaded logs -> https://ci.internal/redwood/rerank/cross-dataset/2141599999 (contains raw score distributions and per-query deltas) :rocket:
sasha: thanks — i'll run the hybrid/importance sweeps today and post updated numbers. tagging @cheng for help with bootstrap harness if you have cycles. :thumbsup:
